subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WebSocket origin gate reusing checkBrowserOrigin

question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` be enforced before upgrade for every WebSocket request carrying `Origin`, or remain limited to the existing browser/Control UI/webchat admission scope?
rationale: The hook runs before protocol client identity is known, so code review cannot safely infer whether rejection of non-UI Origin-bearing and trusted-proxy clients is an intentional security policy change or an upgrade regression.

options.title: Preserve current client-aware scope
options.body: Do not apply the pre-upgrade gate until the Gateway has a safe pre-handshake discriminator that preserves the existing browser/Control UI/webchat policy boundary.

options.title: Approve all-Origin enforcement
options.body: Adopt the broader gateway-client admission contract, document the behavior change, and add regression proof for native/custom-scheme and trusted-proxy scenarios.

recommendation.title: Preserve current client-aware scope
recommendation.body: Do not apply the pre-upgrade gate until the Gateway has a safe pre-handshake discriminator that preserves the existing browser/Control UI/webchat policy boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion routes the current browser-origin enforcement contract to this recent area contributor.
